title: Section-summary nodes for broad questions
description: Index section and paper summaries as retrievable, cited nodes so small-context models can answer broad questions such as 'list all limitations' without the full paper.
acceptance_criteria: Given a broad question on a long paper with a small local model, when answering, then section-summary nodes supply coverage with citations to their source chunks.
verification: Deferred (P2) on 2026-10-09: not implemented on feat/rag-context. Live local answers fit 8-9 passages within the 3,072-token budget; broad questions on long papers remain the open case. On 2026-10-10 it was folded into ARA-094 (retrieval orchestration design); implemented there. Implemented in ARA-094 on 2026-10-10 (hosted models; open models stay frozen): migration 0011_section_summaries; one summary of at most 100 words per top-level body section with at least two passages, written once per reading by a durable section_summaries job with the saved default model and effort (no other model; nothing when summary_blocker refuses), validated against the section's own passages, usage per summary and total cost in the job result; embedded with the library-wide model, re-embedded and pruned with the chunks; existing ready PDFs backfilled once at startup. Summaries are searched beside chunks (keyword and vector) for every question; in an answer a summary has no handle and shows its source chunks' handles, so every citation resolves to a real chunk and page of that paper (sources read only from the chat's pinned PDFs). Tests: 21 cases in test_section_summaries_integration.py plus the migration test. Not measured on the user's papers; no live OpenAI call; the local small-model case of the original criterion is not exercised while open models are frozen.
